cards.title: Core idea
cards.body: PACELC extends CAP. If there is a Partition, choose Availability or Consistency; Else, in normal operation, choose Latency or Consistency. CAP only covers partitions, but most of the time the system is not partitioned.

cards.title: How it works
cards.body: The Else part matters daily: strong consistency means waiting for replicas on every write, costing latency. Cassandra and DynamoDB default to PA/EL; HBase and ZooKeeper are PC/EC. You can choose per operation: fast async writes, strongly consistent reads where needed.

questions.q: Is PACELC a fixed label per database?
questions.a: No. Labels describe defaults; Cassandra with ONE is EL, with QUORUM it behaves EC.

questions.q: Why does the Else case matter more day to day?
questions.a: Systems are rarely partitioned, but every write pays the latency of consistency.
